zh.title: 英國法院對越捷航空頒全球資產凍結令　涉及約2.5億美元租機債務
zh.summary: 英國法院因約2.5億美元未清償判決債務，對越捷航空頒全球資產凍結令。報導指出凍結金額上限約2.516億美元；裁定保留正常營運安排，並非停飛命令。
body: 英國高等法院商事法庭於2026年10月15日，應飛機租賃公司FW Aviation (Holdings) 1 Limited（FWA）聲請，對越南低成本航空公司越捷航空（VietJet Aviation）頒布全球資產凍結令。判決指出，越捷積欠約2.5億美元的判決債務；濠遊天下引述媒體報導，凍結令的金額上限約為2.516億美元。
爭議源於四架Airbus A321客機的租賃融資安排。越捷未付租金後，相關出租融資方於2021年10月發出終止租約通知，FWA隨後取得相關追索權利。英國法院曾於2025年判令越捷支付約1.82億美元，另加利息及費用；其後其他判決款項與費用累積，使待清償金額進一步增加。
本次裁定的核心是資產移轉風險。法院認定，越捷透過與關係企業Angelica Holding Limited（AHL）的安排，移轉大量與未來飛機訂單相關的價值，對債權人執行造成風險。越捷則主張相關交易屬一般航空融資與再融資業務，並反對凍結令；法院審查雙方論點後仍決定核准。
判決亦說明，航空公司的資產不僅是已交付的飛機，還包括未來購機及發動機交付權利、交付前付款、租賃押金與維修儲備金等。這些權益尚未必轉化為可直接扣押的現金或實體資產，因此成為本案跨國追償的重要焦點；不能將凍結令概括解讀為所有租賃飛機已被沒收。
對營運影響，法院指出凍結令草案保留越南境內資產及境外營運資產的正常業務安排。本次裁定屬債務執行程序，並非民航主管機關的停飛命令，也不代表越捷的飛機訂單已取消。後續對資金調度及機隊交付的影響仍須觀察，旅客應依航空公司與機場公布的實際航班動態安排旅程。

en.title: UK Court Grants Worldwide Asset Freeze Against VietJet Over US$250 Million Leasing Debt
en.summary: A UK court granted a worldwide freezing order against VietJet over approximately US$250 million in unpaid judgments. Reports put the cap at US$251.6 million. The ruling provides for ordinary business operations and is not a grounding order.
body: The English High Court's Commercial Court granted a worldwide freezing order against VietJet Aviation on October 15, 2026, on the application of aircraft lessor FW Aviation (Holdings) 1 Limited (FWA). The judgment records approximately US$250 million in unpaid judgment debt. Macau on Journey, citing media reports, puts the freezing-order cap at approximately US$251.6 million.

The dispute concerns financing leases for four Airbus A321 aircraft. Following unpaid rent, termination notices were served in October 2021, and FWA subsequently acquired the relevant recovery rights. A 2025 judgment ordered VietJet to pay approximately US$182 million plus interest and costs. Further judgments and costs increased the outstanding amount.

The latest decision centres on the risk of asset dissipation. The court found that arrangements with related company Angelica Holding Limited (AHL) transferred substantial value associated with future aircraft orders, creating a risk to enforcement. VietJet argued that these were ordinary aviation financing and refinancing transactions and opposed the freezing order. The court considered both sides before granting relief.

The judgment explains that an airline's assets extend beyond delivered aircraft to contractual rights over future aircraft and engine deliveries, pre-delivery payments, lease deposits and maintenance reserves. Such rights may not yet be cash or physical property readily available for seizure, making them important to cross-border recovery. The order should not be read as the confiscation of all leased aircraft.

On operations, the court noted that the draft order accommodated ordinary business involving assets in Vietnam and operational assets overseas. This is a debt-enforcement measure rather than an aviation authority's grounding order, and it does not establish that VietJet's aircraft orders have been cancelled. The effects on financing and deliveries remain to be seen; travellers should follow actual flight updates from the airline and airports.

facts.claim: FWA is seeking to recover more than $250 million in outstanding court judgments.
facts.sourceQuote: FW Aviation Holdings1 Limited (FWA) seeks to recover more than $250 million in outstanding court judgments.

facts.claim: The court found a real risk VietJet could move assets beyond creditors’ reach while FWA continues its recovery efforts.
facts.sourceQuote: The court found that there was a real risk VietJet could move assets out of reach of its creditors while FWA continues its efforts to recover the money.

facts.claim: The dispute began over lease agreements for four Airbus A321 aircraft delivered to VietJet in 2018 and 2019.
facts.sourceQuote: The dispute began over lease agreements for four Airbus A321 aircraft delivered to VietJet in 2018 and 2019 under financing arrangements known as Japanese Operating Leases with Call Options (JOLCO).

facts.claim: Under agreements involving Angelica Holding Limited, VietJet transferred almost all the value of its future aircraft order book to AHL, based on its December 2024 value.
facts.sourceQuote: The latest ruling also examined agreements between VietJet and Angelica Holding Limited (AHL), a related company. Under these agreements, VietJet transferred almost all the value of its future aircraft order book, based on its value in December 2024, to AHL.
